examples.romanization: geu ganguineun daechero ihaehagi swiun pyeonieosseoyo.

entries.nuance: 대체로 gives an overall, big-picture judgment ('on the whole'), acknowledging that small exceptions may exist. Using 대체로 for a single concrete instance; it describes overall tendencies, not one event.
Confusing it with 대체 (= 도대체, 'on earth') used in questions; the meanings are unrelated.

entries.nuance: 일반적으로 introduces a general rule or what is typically the case, much like 'in general' or 'typically.' It is more formal and explanatory than 보통 and is common in writing, explanations, and academic-leaning speech. It often sets up a norm that can later be contrasted with exceptions (예외적으로).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Dropping the -으로 and saying 일반적 alone as an adverb; the adverbial form needs -으로.
Using it for personal habits ('I generally…'); for that, 주로/보통 sound more natural.

Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 특별히 V했어요 ("I did V specially/on purpose") shows how it actually behaves. examples.romanization: oneureun sonnimi osyeoseo teukbyeolhi eumsigeul mani junbihaesseoyo.
examples.en: We have guests today, so I specially prepared a lot of food.

examples.ko: 특별히 가고 싶은 곳은 없어요. 아무 데나 괜찮아요.
examples.romanization: teukbyeolhi gago sipeun goseun eopseoyo. amu dena gwaenchanayo.
examples.en: There's no place I particularly want to go. Anywhere is fine.

examples.ko: 선생님이 저를 특별히 챙겨 주셔서 감사했어요.
examples.romanization: seonsaengnimi jeoreul teukbyeolhi chaenggyeo jusyeoseo gamsahaesseoyo.
examples.en: The teacher looked after me especially well, so I was grateful.

entries.nuance: 특별히 means doing or feeling something in a special, deliberate, or out-of-the-ordinary way, and in negative sentences it softens to 'not particularly.' This contrasts with 특히, which simply singles out one item from a group. Choose 특별히 when the emphasis is on the special manner or intent, and especially favor it in '없어요/않아요' patterns.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 특별히 where you mean 'among these, especially X'; that calls for 특히.
Forgetting that 특별히 + negative is the idiomatic way to say 'not really / nothing in particular.'

In Korean the particle or ending next to 무엇보다 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

Stresses priority in order and importance

examples.en: I think health is more important than anything.
examples.note: Ranks one thing above all others

examples.ko: 여러 이유가 있지만, 무엇보다 가족과 가까워서 이 동네를 골랐어요.
examples.romanization: yeoreo iyuga itjiman, mueotboda gajokgwa gakkawoseo i dongnereul gollasseoyo.
examples.en: There are several reasons, but above all I chose this neighborhood to be near family.

examples.ko: 새 직장은 무엇보다 분위기가 좋아서 마음에 들어요.
examples.romanization: sae jikjangeun mueotboda bunwigiga joaseo maeume deureoyo.
examples.en: I like my new workplace above all because the atmosphere is good.
examples.note: Points to the top factor in a judgment

entries.nuance: 무엇보다 (often 무엇보다도) elevates one point above everything else, like 'above all' or 'more than anything.' It is a natural way to mark your top priority or the most decisive factor when several exist. Slightly emphatic and common in both speech and writing, it pairs especially well with 중요하다 and reasons for a choice.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Treating 무엇보다 as a comparison of two concrete nouns; it ranks one point over all others, not just one rival.
Reading it literally as 'than what'; it functions as a fixed expression meaning 'above all.'

entries.english: never; by no means (with a negative)
entries.shortExplanation: 결코 means "never; by no means (with a negative)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "never; by no means (with a negative)" is 결코 (gyeolko). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 결코 V지 않다 ("never V; by no means V"). Watch the particle attached to 결코 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 결코 V지 않다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 결코.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.en: never V; by no means V
usagePhrases.note: Must be paired with a negative predicate
결코 쉽지 않아요 (by no means easy)
결코 cannot stand with a positive verb
결코 is more written/formal than 절대로

examples.ko: 저는 그 약속을 결코 잊지 않을 거예요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun geu yaksogeul gyeolko itji aneul geoyeyo.
examples.en: I will never forget that promise.
examples.note: Strong, formal negation of a future action

examples.en: This was by no means an easy decision.

examples.ko: 그분은 결코 그런 말을 할 사람이 아니에요.
examples.romanization: geubuneun gyeolko geureon mareul hal sarami anieyo.
examples.en: He is by no means the kind of person who would say that.

entries.nuance: 결코 is an emphatic negative adverb meaning 'never / by no means,' and it must co-occur with a negative ending such as -지 않다 or 아니다. It is more formal and emphatic than 절대로 and is common in writing, declarations, and firm statements. Because it inherently signals negation, sentences feel incomplete or wrong if the predicate is positive.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Pairing 결코 with an affirmative predicate; it requires a negative (-지 않다/아니다/없다).
Using it casually in light conversation where 절대(로) or 전혀 would sound more natural.

usagePhrases.en: after a long N, at last
usagePhrases.note: Often follows a phrase of long effort/waiting

examples.ko: 몇 년 동안 준비한 끝에 마침내 시험에 합격했어요.
examples.romanization: myeon nyeon dongan junbihan kkeute machimnae siheome hapgyeokaesseoyo.
examples.en: After years of preparation, I finally passed the exam.
examples.note: Marks the climactic result of long effort

examples.en: The long-awaited news finally arrived.

examples.ko: 여러 번 실패했지만 마침내 원하던 결과를 얻었어요.
examples.romanization: yeoreo beon silpaehaetjiman machimnae wonhadeon gyeolgwareul eodeosseoyo.

entries.nuance: 마침내 means 'finally/at last' and frames an outcome as the culmination of a long process, effort, or wait. commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 마침내 for trivial 'and then finally' sequencing; it implies a significant, awaited result.
Confusing it with 마침 ('as it happens / just in time'), which has a different meaning.

entries.shortExplanation: 반대로 means "on the contrary; conversely; the other way around" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 반대로 (bandaero) means "on the contrary; conversely; the other way around". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is A. 반대로 B. ("A. Conversely, B."). In Korean the particle or ending next to 반대로 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 반대로 하다 = do it the other way around
Marks a contrast with a stated reference

examples.ko: 형은 활발한데, 반대로 동생은 아주 조용해요.
examples.romanization: hyeongeun hwalbalhande, bandaero dongsaengeun aju joyonghaeyo.
examples.en: The older brother is outgoing; conversely, the younger one is very quiet.

examples.ko: 쉬울 거라고 생각했는데 반대로 정말 어려웠어요.
examples.romanization: swiul georago saenggakaenneunde bandaero jeongmal eoryeowosseoyo.
examples.en: I thought it would be easy, but on the contrary it was really hard.

examples.ko: 설명서와 반대로 조립해서 다시 해야 했어요.
examples.romanization: seolmyeongseowa bandaero joripaeseo dasi haeya haesseoyo.
examples.en: I assembled it the opposite way from the manual, so I had to redo it.

entries.nuance: 반대로 introduces an opposite case or a reversal, covering both 'on the contrary' (contrasting facts) and 'the other way around' (reversed manner/direction). It is more concrete than the abstract connector 반면(에), often pointing to a literal opposite action or a flipped expectation. Use it to flip a statement, contrast two parties, or describe doing something in reverse.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 반대로 only as a pure clause-connector where 반면(에) fits; 반대로 leans toward a literal opposite.
Forgetting the marker in 'N과/와 반대로' when contrasting with a specific reference point.

entries.explanation: 한마디로 (hanmadiro) = "in a word; in short; to put it simply". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 한마디로 N이다 ("in a word, it's N") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 한마디로, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.

entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: Sums up with a single label

usagePhrases.en: to put it in one word
usagePhrases.note: Common fuller form before a summary
한마디로 is punchier and more spoken

examples.en: That movie was, in a word, a waste of time.
examples.note: Compresses a judgment into one phrase

examples.en: To put it simply, we just weren't prepared enough.
The new system is, in short, fair to everyone.

entries.nuance: 한마디로 means 'in a word / in short' and signals that you are about to condense everything into one blunt summary or label. It is conversational and often a bit emphatic or evaluative, used right before delivering your bottom line. Compared with the more neutral 요약하면, 한마디로 sounds punchier and more opinionated.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Following 한마디로 with a long, multi-clause explanation; it promises a short, single takeaway.
Reading it literally as 'with one word said'; it works as a fixed discourse marker meaning 'in short.'

entries.shortExplanation: 사업 means "business; enterprise; venture" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 사업 (saeop) means "business; enterprise; venture". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 사업을 하다 ("to run a business"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 사업 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about talking about work, schedules, tasks, and obligations, then change a single part.

entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about talking about work, schedules, tasks, and obligations. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 사업하다 also works as one verb; 사업을 하다 splits it with the object marker
시작하다 = to begin; common with launching a venture
잘되다 (one word) = to go well; 사업이 안되다 = to do badly
계획 = plan; 사업 모델, 사업 분야 also use 사업 as a modifier

examples.ko: 저는 작은 온라인 사업을 시작하려고 해요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun jageun ollain saeobeul sijakaryeogo haeyo.
examples.en: I'm planning to start a small online business.
examples.note: V-(으)려고 하다 = intend to; 작은 modifies 사업

examples.ko: 요즘 경기가 안 좋아서 사업이 잘 안돼요.
examples.romanization: yojeum gyeonggiga an joaseo saeobi jal andwaeyo.
examples.en: Business isn't going well these days because the economy is bad.
examples.note: 안돼요 = isn't going well; -아서/어서 gives the reason

examples.en: He's someone who succeeded big in business.
examples.note: 사업으로 = through/in business; 성공하다 = to succeed

entries.nuance: 사업 is business as an undertaking or venture — running a company, a commercial project, or being self-employed. It is broader and more concrete than 산업 (industry as a sector) and refers to what an individual or company actively does. A government or public project is also called 사업 (예: 복지 사업, welfare project).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Don't confuse 사업 (a business/venture you run) with 산업 (an industry sector like 자동차 산업).
사업하다 is one verb, but when you add an object marker you must split it: 사업을 하다, not 사업하다를.

entries.shortExplanation: 산업 means "industry (sector of the economy)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "industry (sector of the economy)" is 산업 (saneop). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 자동차 산업 ("the automobile industry"). Watch the particle attached to 산업 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. usagePhrases.note: 산업 follows the field as a modifier: 반도체 산업, 관광 산업
발전하다 = to develop/advance; 산업이 성장하다 also common
구조 = structure; describes how an economy's sectors are organized
첨단 = cutting-edge; contrasts with 전통 산업 (traditional industry)

examples.ko: 한국은 반도체 산업이 매우 발달해 있어요.
examples.romanization: hangugeun bandoche saneobi maeu baldalhae isseoyo.
examples.en: Korea's semiconductor industry is very advanced.
examples.note: 발달해 있다 = is (in a state of being) developed; V-아/어 있다 for resulting state

examples.ko: 요즘은 인공지능 관련 산업이 빠르게 성장하고 있어요.
examples.romanization: yojeumeun ingongjineung gwallyeon saneobi ppareuge seongjanghago isseoyo.
examples.en: These days AI-related industries are growing fast.
examples.note: 관련 = related; -고 있다 for ongoing change

examples.en: This city is famous for its tourism industry.

entries.nuance: 산업 refers to an industry as a whole sector of the economy (manufacturing, tourism, IT), not a single company. Use it for macro-level talk about the economy. 사업 is what a specific business does; 산업 is the field that many businesses belong to. You will see it constantly in news and formal writing.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
산업 is a sector, so don't say 산업을 시작하다 to mean 'start a business' — use 사업을 시작하다.
Avoid the romanization-driven mix-up: 산업 = industry, 사업 = business; the 'ㄴ' vs 'ㅏ' difference matters.

number + 년 after 경력 states length of career
-직 = position; contrasts with 신입 (new graduate hire)

examples.ko: 이 일은 관련 경력이 3년 이상 필요해요.
examples.romanization: i ireun gwallyeon gyeongnyeogi 3nyeon isang piryohaeyo.

examples.ko: 저는 마케팅 분야에서 경력을 쌓고 싶어요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun maketing bunyaeseo gyeongnyeogeul ssako sipeoyo.

examples.note: 분야에서 = in the field of; -고 싶다 = want to

examples.note: -(으)ㄹ수록 = the more...the more; 높아지다 = to become higher

entries.nuance: 경력 means accumulated professional experience or work history — what goes on a résumé. It differs from 경험 (경험, any experience, including everyday or one-time experiences). commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Don't swap 경력 with 경험: 경력 = professional track record, 경험 = experience in general (already in beginner vocab).
경력 is counted in years with 년 (경력 3년), not with 번 or 개.

Don't confuse 수입 (income/imports) with 수출 (exports); 입 = enter, 출 = exit.

입다 = to suffer (formal); 손해를 끼치다 = to cause loss to someone

examples.ko: 지금 팔면 손해를 볼 것 같아서 좀 더 기다리려고요.
examples.romanization: jigeum palmyeon sonhaereul bol geot gataseo jom deo gidariryeogoyo.
examples.en: I think I'll lose money if I sell now, so I'm going to wait a bit longer.
examples.note: V-(으)ㄹ 것 같다 = seems like; -(으)려고요 = I intend to

examples.ko: 회사가 이번 투자로 큰 손해를 입었어요.
examples.romanization: hoesaga ibeon tujaro keun sonhaereul ibeosseoyo.

examples.ko: 환불해 주지 않으면 소비자가 손해를 봐요.
examples.romanization: hwanbulhae juji aneumyeon sobijaga sonhaereul bwayo.
examples.en: If they don't refund it, the consumer takes the loss.
examples.note: -아/어 주다 = do for someone; 소비자 = consumer

entries.nuance: 손해 is a loss or damage, almost always financial or in terms of disadvantage — the opposite of 이익/이득 (profit/gain). Use 손해를 보다 (with 보다) for 'to suffer a loss' — learners often wrongly say 손해를 하다.
손해 is about loss/disadvantage; don't use it for physical breakage (use 고장/피해).

entries.explanation: 가치 (gachi) means "value; worth". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 가치가 있다 ("to be worthwhile / have value"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 가치 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about talking about work, schedules, tasks, and obligations, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: 오르다/떨어지다 for value going up/down (e.g., property, stocks)
예: 볼 가치가 있다 = worth seeing

examples.romanization: i gyeongheomeun doneuro sal su eopsneun gachiga isseoyo.
examples.en: This experience has a value that money can't buy.
examples.note: V-(으)ㄹ 수 없다 = cannot; 가치가 있다 = has value

examples.ko: 그 그림은 시간이 지날수록 가치가 올라갔어요.
examples.romanization: geu geurimeun sigani jinalsurok gachiga ollagasseoyo.
examples.en: That painting rose in value as time passed.
examples.note: -(으)ㄹ수록 = the more...; 올라가다 = to go up

examples.ko: 저는 일을 고를 때 연봉보다 가치를 더 중요하게 생각해요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun ireul goreul ttae yeonbongboda gachireul deo jungyohage saenggakaeyo.
examples.en: When I choose a job, I value meaning more than salary.
examples.note: 고를 때 = when choosing; 중요하게 생각하다 = to consider important

entries.nuance: 가치 means value or worth — both economic value (가치가 오르다, rises in value) and abstract worth (인생의 가치, the value of life). The pattern V-(으)ㄹ 가치가 있다 ('worth doing') is extremely useful. 가치관 (one's values/worldview) is a high-frequency derived word. Distinguish from 가격 (가격, price tag) and 값 (value/cost), which are concrete amounts.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Don't confuse 가치 (worth/value, abstract or economic) with 가격 (the listed price, already in vocab).
For 'worth doing', use V-(으)ㄹ 가치가 있다, not 가치가 하다.

examples.ko: 가격은 조금 비싸지만 품질이 정말 좋아요.
examples.romanization: gagyeogeun jogeum bissajiman pumjiri jeongmal joayo.
examples.en: It's a bit pricey, but the quality is really good.

examples.ko: 요즘 소비자들은 가격보다 품질을 더 따져요.
examples.romanization: yojeum sobijadeureun gagyeokboda pumjireul deo ttajyeoyo.
examples.en: These days consumers scrutinize quality more than price.
examples.note: 따지다 (already in vocab) = to scrutinize; N보다 더 = more than

examples.ko: 품질을 높이려면 생산 과정을 개선해야 해요.
examples.romanization: pumjireul nopiryeomyeon saengsan gwajeongeul gaeseonhaeya haeyo.
examples.en: To improve quality, you need to improve the production process.
examples.note: -(으)려면 = if you want to; -아/어야 하다 = must

entries.nuance: 품질 refers specifically to the quality of goods or products — how well-made something is. It is the standard word in 품질 관리 (quality control) and product reviews. Don't use 품질 for the quality of an abstract thing like life or sleep; for those Koreans say 삶의 질 or 수면의 질 (using 질, quality). 품(品) signals 'goods', so 품질 = goods-quality.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Use 품질 for product quality, but 삶의 질 (not 삶의 품질) for 'quality of life'.
품질이 좋다/나쁘다 describes quality; 품질을 잘하다 is wrong (it's a noun state, not an action).

entries.shortExplanation: 생산 means "production; manufacturing" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 생산 (saengsan) = "production; manufacturing". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 생산하다 ("to produce/manufacture") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 생산, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about talking about work, schedules, tasks, and obligations and swap just one element to make it yours.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 생산하다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 생산.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about talking about work, schedules, tasks, and obligations. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 대량 = large quantity; 소량 생산 = small-batch production
라인, 과정 follow 생산 as compounds

examples.ko: 이 공장에서는 하루에 자동차를 천 대 생산해요.
examples.romanization: i gongjangeseoneun harue jadongchareul cheon dae saengsanhaeyo.
examples.en: This factory produces a thousand cars a day.
examples.note: 에서는 = at (location, topic); 대 = counter for vehicles

examples.ko: 원자재 가격이 올라서 생산 비용이 늘었어요.
examples.romanization: wonjajae gagyeogi ollaseo saengsan biyongi neureosseoyo.
examples.en: Production costs rose because raw material prices went up.
examples.note: 원자재 = raw materials; 비용 (already in vocab) = cost

examples.ko: 수요가 많아지면 생산을 더 늘려야 해요.
examples.romanization: suyoga manajimyeon saengsaneul deo neullyeoya haeyo.
examples.en: When demand grows, you have to increase production.

entries.nuance: 생산 means production or manufacturing — making goods. It pairs naturally with 소비 (consumption) as the supply side of the economy (생산과 소비). Use 대량 생산 for mass production. The agent who produces is a 생산자 (producer), opposite of 소비자 (consumer). Keep 생산 (making things) distinct from 산업 (the industry sector) and 사업 (a business venture).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.

entries.nuance: 자본 is capital in the economic sense — the money and assets used to run or start a business. 안도의 한숨을 쉬다 = to sigh in relief

examples.ko: 검사 결과가 정상이라는 말에 안도의 한숨을 쉬었어요.
examples.romanization: geomsa gyeolgwaga jeongsangiraneun mare andoui hansumeul swieosseoyo.
examples.en: At the word that the test results were normal, I let out a sigh of relief.
examples.note: 안도의 한숨을 쉬다 = to sigh in relief

examples.ko: 아이가 무사히 집에 도착해서 그제야 안도했어요.
examples.romanization: aiga musahi jibe dochakaeseo geujeya andohaesseoyo.
examples.en: My child got home safely, and only then did I feel relieved.

examples.romanization: iri jal kkeunnatdaneun sosige keun andogameul neukkyeosseoyo.

entries.nuance: 안도 is relief, the loosening of tension once a worry or danger has passed. The signature phrase is 안도의 한숨을 쉬다 ('to breathe a sigh of relief'), and 안도감 names the felt emotion. It is a bit more written and composed than the casual 다행이다 ('what a relief'), which is what you'd blurt out in conversation.

Using 안도 in casual speech where 다행이다 is more natural
Confusing 안도 (relief after worry) with 안심 (feeling secure/at ease going forward)

examples.ko: 비가 며칠째 와서 그런지 기분이 좀 우울해요.
examples.romanization: biga myeochiljjae waseo geureonji gibuni jom uulhaeyo.
examples.en: Maybe because it's rained for days, I feel a bit down.

examples.ko: 요즘 별일 없는데도 우울감이 자주 들어요.
examples.romanization: yojeum byeoril eopsneundedo uulgami jaju deureoyo.

examples.ko: 우울할 땐 햇빛을 좀 쐬는 게 도움이 돼요.
examples.romanization: uulhal ttaen haetbicheul jom ssoeneun ge doumi dwaeyo.
examples.en: When I feel down, getting some sunlight helps.

entries.nuance: 우울 most often appears as the adjective 우울하다 ('to feel down, gloomy'), the everyday word for a low mood. Be careful to separate the passing feeling 우울하다/우울감 from 우울증, which is clinical depression as a diagnosed condition. Korean 20-30s use 우울하다 freely for ordinary blue days, much like English 'I feel down.'

Calling a passing low mood 우울증; that word means clinical depression as an illness
Saying 우울다; the adjective is 우울하다, and the casual form is 우울해요

Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

usagePhrases.note: formal; to appeal that one was wronged

examples.ko: 하지도 않은 일로 혼나서 너무 억울했어요.
examples.romanization: hajido aneun illo honnaseo neomu eogulhaesseoyo.
examples.en: I got scolded for something I didn't even do, so it felt so unfair.

examples.ko: 제 잘못이 아닌데 오해를 받아서 억울함이 컸어요.
examples.romanization: je jalmosi aninde ohaereul badaseo eogulhami keosseoyo.
examples.en: It wasn't my fault but I was misunderstood, so the sense of injustice was great.

examples.ko: 억울하면 참지 말고 차분히 설명하는 게 좋아요.
examples.romanization: eogulhamyeon chamji malgo chabunhi seolmyeonghaneun ge joayo.
examples.en: If you feel wronged, it's better to explain calmly than to bottle it up.

entries.nuance: 억울함 is the very Korean feeling of being unfairly blamed or wronged, the frustration of being misjudged when you did nothing wrong. The adjective 억울하다 is extremely common in daily speech (억울해요!). There is no tidy English equivalent, which makes it a valuable word; it centers on injustice done to you, unlike plain 화 (anger).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Equating it with simple anger; 억울함 specifically means feeling unjustly wronged
Using 억울함 for general unfairness in the world; it's about a wrong done to you personally, while 불공평 is broad unfairness

entries.shortExplanation: 수치심 means "shame; sense of disgrace" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "shame; sense of disgrace" is 수치심 (suchisim). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 수치심 ("shame / disgrace"). Watch the particle attached to 수치심 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 수치심. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 수치심.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: deep shame over loss of dignity

examples.ko: 많은 사람들 앞에서 실수해서 수치심을 느꼈어요.
examples.romanization: maneun saramdeul apeseo silsuhaeseo suchisimeul neukkyeosseoyo.
examples.en: I made a mistake in front of many people, so I felt ashamed.
When the lie was exposed, I was overcome with shame.

examples.ko: 남을 함부로 대하는 건 정말 수치스러운 일이에요.
examples.romanization: nameul hamburo daehaneun geon jeongmal suchiseureoun irieyo.
examples.en: Treating others carelessly is a truly shameful thing.

entries.nuance: 수치심 is heavy, dignity-wounding shame, far stronger than the everyday 부끄러움 (mild embarrassment). It is the deep disgrace of having one's pride or honor damaged, and shows up in serious contexts. For blushing over a small social slip, use 부끄럽다 or 창피하다; reserve 수치심 for genuine, weighty shame.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 수치심 for mild embarrassment; that's 부끄러움 or 창피함, while 수치심 is grave shame
Saying 수치심하다; pair the noun with 느끼다/들다, and use 수치스럽다 for the adjective

entries.explanation: 질병 (jilbyeong) = "disease, illness (formal, general term)". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 질병을 예방하다 ("to prevent disease") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 질병, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. usagePhrases.en: to come down with a disease

examples.ko: 손을 자주 씻으면 여러 질병을 예방할 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: soneul jaju ssiseumyeon yeoreo jilbyeongeul yebanghal su isseoyo.
examples.en: If you wash your hands often, you can prevent many diseases.

examples.ko: 요즘은 생활 습관 때문에 생기는 질병이 많아요.
examples.romanization: yojeumeun saenghwal seupgwan ttaemune saenggineun jilbyeongi manayo.
examples.en: These days there are many diseases caused by lifestyle habits.

examples.ko: 그 병원은 희귀 질병을 전문으로 치료해요.
examples.romanization: geu byeongwoneun huigwi jilbyeongeul jeonmuneuro chiryohaeyo.
examples.en: That hospital specializes in treating rare diseases.
examples.note: 희귀 질병 = rare disease, 격식 있는 의료 맥락

entries.nuance: 질병은 '병'을 격식 있게 이르는 한자어로, 뉴스·보건·의학 문서에서 폭넓게 쓰인다. 일상 대화에서는 그냥 '병'(병에 걸리다)이라고 하지만, '질병 예방, 만성 질병'처럼 공식적이거나 일반적인 개념을 말할 때는 질병이 자연스럽다. 특정 증상 하나가 아니라 병이라는 큰 범주를 가리킨다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
친구끼리 가벼운 대화에서 '질병에 걸렸어'라고 하는 것 — 일상에서는 '병에 걸렸어, 아파'가 더 자연스럽고 질병은 격식체다.
증상(symptom)과 혼동하는 것 — 질병은 병 자체, 증상은 그 병으로 나타나는 기침·열 같은 표시다.

entries.explanation: 증상 (jeungsang) means "symptom". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 증상이 나타나다 ("symptoms appear"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 증상 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs, then change a single part.

examples.en: When did these symptoms start appearing?

examples.ko: 약을 먹었는데도 증상이 전혀 나아지지 않아요.
examples.romanization: yageul meogeonneundedo jeungsangi jeonhyeo naajiji anayo.
examples.en: Even though I took medicine, the symptoms aren't getting better at all.

examples.ko: 초기에는 증상이 가벼워서 그냥 넘어가기 쉬워요.
examples.romanization: chogieneun jeungsangi gabyeowoseo geunyang neomeogagi swiwoyo.
examples.en: In the early stage the symptoms are mild, so it's easy to just let them slide.
examples.note: 초기 증상 = early symptoms, 흔한 설명

entries.nuance: 증상은 병 때문에 몸에 나타나는 기침·열·통증 같은 '표시'를 가리킨다. 병 자체인 질병과 달리, 증상은 겉으로 드러나는 신호라서 병원에서 '어떤 증상이 있으세요?'처럼 물을 때 핵심 단어가 된다. '증상이 있다/나타나다/심해지다/사라지다'로 그 변화를 표현하면 자연스럽다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.

'증상을 느끼다'만 쓰는 것 — '증상이 있다, 증상이 나타나다'처럼 증상을 주어로 말하는 게 더 자연스러운 경우가 많다.

examples.ko: 허리에 통증이 있어서 오래 앉아 있기가 힘들어요.

examples.romanization: susul hueneun myeochil dongan tongjeungi isseul su isseoyo.

entries.shortExplanation: 부상 means "injury (from accident, sports, etc.)" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 부상 (busang) means "injury (from accident, sports, etc.)". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 부상을 입다 ("to sustain an injury"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 부상 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs, then change a single part.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 부상을 입다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 부상.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 경기 중에 큰 부상을 입어서 한동안 못 뛰어요.
examples.romanization: geu seonsuneun gyeonggi junge keun busangeul ibeoseo handongan mot ttwieoyo.
examples.en: That player sustained a serious injury during the game, so he can't play for a while.
Fortunately, there were no major injuries in the accident.

examples.ko: 부상에서 완전히 회복하는 데 두 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.romanization: busangeseo wanjeonhi hoebokaneun de du dari geollyeosseoyo.
examples.en: It took two months to fully recover from the injury.

entries.nuance: 부상은 사고·운동·충돌 등으로 몸을 '다친 것'을 가리키는 한자어로, 뉴스나 스포츠 보도에서 특히 자주 쓰인다. 일상 대화의 '다쳤어요'를 명사로 격식 있게 표현한 말이며, '부상을 입다/당하다'가 표준이다. 병 때문이 아니라 외부 충격으로 생긴 손상이라는 점이 질병과 다르다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
'부상을 하다'라고 하는 것 — '부상을 입다, 부상을 당하다, 다치다'가 자연스럽다.
병으로 아픈 것에 부상을 쓰는 것 — 부상은 사고·충격으로 다친 것이고, 병은 질병이라고 구분해야 한다.

entries.shortExplanation: 수술 means "surgery, operation" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "surgery, operation" is 수술 (susul). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 수술을 받다 ("to undergo surgery"). examples.ko: 할아버지가 다음 주에 무릎 수술을 받으세요.
examples.romanization: harabeojiga daeum jue mureup susureul badeuseyo.
examples.en: My grandfather is having knee surgery next week.

examples.ko: 수술은 잘됐지만 회복하는 데 시간이 좀 걸린대요.
examples.romanization: susureun jaldwaetjiman hoebokaneun de sigani jom geollindaeyo.
examples.en: The surgery went well, but they say recovery will take some time.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 수술밖에 방법이 없다고 하셨어요.
examples.romanization: uisa seonsaengnimi susulbakke bangbeobi eopsdago hasyeosseoyo.
examples.en: The doctor said surgery is the only option.

entries.nuance: 수술은 몸을 째거나 손대어 병·부상을 고치는 의료 처치를 뜻한다. 환자 입장에서는 '수술을 받다', 의사가 집도하면 '수술을 하다'로 쓰는데, 일상에서는 둘 다 흔히 들린다. 가벼운 약물 '치료'와 달리 더 크고 직접적인 처치라, '수술밖에 없다, 수술이 필요하다'처럼 심각성을 담아 말한다.

examples.ko: 검사 결과가 나와야 정확한 진단을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: geomsa gyeolgwaga nawaya jeonghwakan jindaneul badeul su isseoyo.
examples.en: You can get an accurate diagnosis only after the test results come out.
examples.note: 검사와 진단의 순서를 보여 주는 문장

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 감기가 아니라 폐렴이라고 진단을 내렸어요.
examples.romanization: uisa seonsaengnimi gamgiga anira pyeryeomirago jindaneul naeryeosseoyo.

examples.ko: 한 병원의 진단만 믿지 말고 다른 곳도 가 보세요.
examples.romanization: han byeongwonui jindanman mitji malgo dareun gotdo ga boseyo.
examples.en: Don't just trust one hospital's diagnosis; try another place too.

entries.nuance: 진단은 의사가 증상과 검사를 바탕으로 '무슨 병인지 판단하는 것'을 뜻한다. 환자는 '진단을 받다', 의사는 '진단을 내리다'로 쓰며, 잘못된 판단은 '오진'이라는 한 단어로 표현한다. 검사(원인을 알아보려 살펴봄) 다음에 진단(결론)이 나오는 흐름을 알아 두면 병원 대화가 한결 쉬워진다.

In Korean the particle or ending next to 검사 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. entries.nuance: 검사는 몸 상태나 원인을 '살펴보고 확인하는 과정'을 뜻한다. 진단(결론)에 앞서 이루어지는 단계라, '검사를 받다 → 검사 결과가 나오다 → 진단을 받다'로 이어진다. 병원에서는 '혈액 검사, 소변 검사, 정밀 검사'처럼 종류를 앞에 붙여 쓰며, 학교 시험을 뜻하는 '시험'과는 다른 단어다.

검사와 진단을 혼동하는 것 — 검사는 알아보는 과정, 진단은 그 결과로 내리는 판단이다.

entries.explanation: "(medical) prescription" is 처방 (cheobang). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 약을 처방하다 ("to prescribe medicine"). examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 일주일치 약을 처방해 주셨어요.
examples.romanization: uisa seonsaengnimi iljuilchi yageul cheobanghae jusyeosseoyo.
examples.en: The doctor prescribed a week's worth of medicine.

entries.nuance: 처방은 의사가 환자에게 '어떤 약을 얼마나 먹을지 정해 주는 것'을 뜻한다. 동사는 '처방하다(의사)', 받는 쪽은 '처방을 받다'이며, 약국에 내는 종이는 '처방전'이라고 구분한다. 한국에서는 전문의약품을 사려면 반드시 처방이 필요해, '처방을 받아야 살 수 있다'는 말을 자주 듣는다.

entries.shortExplanation: 면역력 means "immunity, immune strength" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 면역력 (myeonyeongnyeok) = "immunity, immune strength". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 면역력이 강하다 / 약하다 ("to have strong / weak immunity") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 면역력, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs and swap just one element to make it yours.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 면역력이 강하다 / 약하다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 면역력.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about saying what hurts, asking for rest, and explaining basic health needs. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

examples.ko: 잠을 못 자고 무리했더니 면역력이 떨어진 것 같아요.
examples.romanization: jameul mot jago murihaetdeoni myeonyeongnyeogi tteoreojin geot gatayo.
examples.en: I didn't sleep and overdid it, so I think my immunity has dropped.

examples.ko: 골고루 잘 먹고 운동하면 면역력이 높아져요.
examples.romanization: golgoru jal meokgo undonghamyeon myeonyeongnyeogi nopajyeoyo.
examples.en: If you eat a balanced diet and exercise, your immunity goes up.

examples.ko: 면역력이 약한 사람은 독감에 더 쉽게 걸려요.
examples.romanization: myeonyeongnyeogi yakan sarameun dokgame deo swipge geollyeoyo.
examples.en: People with weak immunity catch the flu more easily.

entries.nuance: 면역력은 몸이 병균과 싸워 이겨 내는 '저항하는 힘'을 뜻하며, '면역(免疫)'에 힘 력(力)이 붙은 말이다. 건강 대화에서 '면역력이 떨어지다/높아지다, 면역력을 키우다'처럼 힘의 세기로 표현하는 것이 핵심이다. 면역력이 약해지면 감염이나 질병에 더 쉽게 노출된다는 맥락으로 자주 쓰인다.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.

면역력을 '많다/적다'로만 표현하는 것 — '면역력이 강하다/약하다, 높다/낮다'가 더 자연스럽다.

entries.shortExplanation: 감염 means "infection" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 감염 (gamyeom) means "infection". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 감염되다 ("to get infected"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 감염 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. examples.en: If you don't disinfect the wound well, it can get infected.

examples.ko: 손을 자주 씻는 것이 감염을 막는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.romanization: soneul jaju ssinneun geosi gamyeomeul mangneun de doumi dwaeyo.

entries.nuance: 감염은 병균·바이러스가 몸에 '들어와 퍼지는 것'을 뜻한다. 보통 수동형 '감염되다'로 많이 쓰며, 무엇에 감염됐는지는 '~에 감염되다'로 표시한다. 단순히 다친 부상과 달리 병원체가 원인이라는 점이 핵심이고, 예방·면역력·합병증과 자연스럽게 이어지는 의료 핵심어다.

examples.ko: 당뇨를 잘 관리하지 않으면 여러 합병증이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: dangnyoreul jal gwallihaji aneumyeon yeoreo hapbyeongjeungi saenggil su isseoyo.
examples.en: If you don't manage diabetes well, various complications can develop.

examples.ko: 수술 자체보다 합병증이 더 위험할 수도 있어요.
examples.romanization: susul jacheboda hapbyeongjeungi deo wiheomhal sudo isseoyo.
examples.en: Complications can sometimes be more dangerous than the surgery itself.
The flu led to pneumonia as a complication.

entries.nuance: 합병증은 하나의 병이나 수술 뒤에 '딸려서 새로 생기는 다른 병이나 문제'를 뜻한다. 원래 병보다 합병증이 더 위험할 때도 많아, '합병증이 생기다/오다, 합병증을 막다'처럼 경계하는 맥락에서 자주 쓰인다. 특히 당뇨·고혈압 같은 만성질환 관리 이야기에서 핵심 단어로 등장한다.

entries.nuance: 응급은 '급해서 바로 손을 써야 하는' 의료 상황을 가리키며, 단독보다 '응급실, 응급 상황, 응급 처치, 응급 환자'처럼 다른 말과 붙여 쓰는 경우가 대부분이다. 한국에서는 위급할 때 119로 전화하고 '응급실'로 간다는 점을 함께 알아 두면 실제 상황에서 바로 통한다. 천천히 받는 일반 진료와 대비되는 긴박함이 핵심이다.

entries.shortExplanation: 의사소통 means "communication" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 의사소통 (uisasotong) means "communication". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 의사소통이 잘 되다 ("to communicate well"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 의사소통 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 의사소통이 잘 되다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 의사소통.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 되다 ('work out') is the natural verb; 의사소통이 잘 돼요 = communication goes well.
Common in workplace and relationship contexts.
원활하다 ('smooth, fluid') is the set adjective that pairs with 의사소통.
능력 ('ability') makes a common compound, especially in job ads.

examples.ko: 외국에서는 언어 때문에 의사소통이 어려울 때가 많아요.
examples.romanization: oegugeseoneun eoneo ttaemune uisasotongi eoryeoul ttaega manayo.
examples.en: Abroad, communication is often difficult because of the language.
examples.note: 의사소통이 어렵다 = 'communication is hard'; 때가 많다 = 'there are many times when'.

examples.ko: 부서 간의 원활한 의사소통이 무엇보다 중요해요.
examples.romanization: buseo ganui wonhwalhan uisasotongi mueotboda jungyohaeyo.
examples.en: Smooth communication between departments is more important than anything.
examples.note: 부서 간 = 'between departments'; 무엇보다 = 'more than anything'.

examples.en: To reduce misunderstandings, honest communication is needed.
examples.note: 줄이려면 = 'in order to reduce'; 필요하다 pairs naturally with 의사소통.

entries.nuance: 의사소통 is the formal, slightly academic word for 'communication' as the exchange of thoughts and intentions (의사 = intention + 소통 = flowing through). In casual speech Koreans often shorten it to 소통, especially when praising someone for being open and approachable (소통이 잘 된다). Reserve 의사소통 for fuller, more written or professional registers.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 대화 ('conversation') when you mean 'communication' as a skill or process — 의사소통 is the broader concept, 대화 is a specific talk.
Saying 의사소통을 하다 too literally; Koreans more often say 의사소통이 잘 되다/안 되다 to describe whether it works.

entries.shortExplanation: 토론 means "debate; structured discussion" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "debate; structured discussion" is 토론 (toron). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 토론을 하다 ("to hold a debate / discuss"). Watch the particle attached to 토론 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 토론을 하다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 토론.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 하다 is the standard verb; 토론하다 also works as one word.
벌어지다 ('unfold, break out') is natural for a lively debate.
찬반 ('for and against') is the set modifier for a two-sided debate.
주제 ('topic') makes a common compound for what is being debated.

examples.ko: 수업 시간에 환경 문제에 대해 토론을 했어요.
examples.romanization: sueop sigane hwangyeong munjee daehae toroneul haesseoyo.
examples.en: In class we had a debate about environmental issues.
examples.note: ~에 대해 토론을 하다 = 'have a debate about ~', the core pattern.

examples.ko: 이 주제는 찬반 토론을 하기에 아주 좋아요.
examples.romanization: i jujeneun chanban toroneul hagie aju joayo.
examples.en: This topic is great for a pro-and-con debate.

examples.ko: 토론에서는 상대방의 의견도 끝까지 들어야 해요.
examples.romanization: toroneseoneun sangdaebangui uigyeondo kkeutkkaji deureoya haeyo.
examples.en: In a debate you have to listen to the other side's opinion to the end.
examples.note: 상대방 = 'the other party'; 끝까지 = 'to the end'.

entries.nuance: 토론 is an organized, rule-based discussion where people exchange and defend opinions on a set topic — think classroom debates, panel discussions, or formal meetings. It is more structured and goal-oriented than 대화 (everyday conversation) and calmer than 논쟁 (a heated dispute). A good 토론 is respectful even when people disagree.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 토론 (a structured debate) with 논쟁 (a heated argument); 토론 aims to exchange views, 논쟁 implies conflict.
Using 토론 for a casual chat with friends — that is 대화 or 이야기, not 토론.

Memorize one useful chunk: 토론을 하다.
Notice which particle, place marker, or ending appears around the word.
Make one personal sentence by changing only one noun, place, time, or adjective.

lesson.pronunciationTip: 토론 is written toron. Use audio and Hangul together because romanization is only a helper.

entries.shortExplanation: 논쟁 means "argument; controversy; dispute" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 논쟁 (nonjaeng) = "argument; controversy; dispute". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 논쟁을 벌이다 ("to engage in / wage an argument") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 논쟁, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 논쟁을 벌이다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 논쟁.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.en: to engage in / wage an argument
usagePhrases.note: 벌이다 ('start, wage') is the idiomatic verb for an active dispute.
일어나다 ('arise') is natural when a dispute breaks out.
뜨겁다 ('hot') is the set modifier; 뜨거운 논쟁 = a fierce debate.

usagePhrases.en: to be open to dispute / debatable
usagePhrases.note: 여지 ('room') in a fixed phrase meaning 'there is room for argument'.

examples.en: That remark sparked a big controversy.
examples.note: 논쟁을 불러일으키다 = 'spark a controversy', a strong written collocation.

examples.ko: 인터넷에서 그 문제를 두고 뜨거운 논쟁이 벌어졌어요.
examples.romanization: inteoneseseo geu munjereul dugo tteugeoun nonjaengi beoreojyeosseoyo.
examples.en: A heated argument broke out online over that issue.

examples.ko: 이건 논쟁의 여지가 없는 명백한 사실이에요.
examples.romanization: igeon nonjaengui yeojiga eopsneun myeongbaekan sasirieyo.
examples.en: This is an obvious fact that leaves no room for dispute.
examples.note: 논쟁의 여지가 없다 = 'no room for argument'; 명백하다 = 'obvious'.

entries.nuance: 논쟁 is a heated argument or public controversy in which sides clash, often emotionally or over high-stakes issues. It is sharper and more adversarial than 토론 (a structured debate) and broader than a personal quarrel (싸움). A topic that is 논쟁적이다 ('controversial') tends to divide people strongly.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Treating 논쟁 and 토론 as the same — 논쟁 carries conflict and friction, 토론 is an orderly exchange of views.
Using 논쟁 for a personal fight between friends; that is usually 싸움 or 다툼, while 논쟁 is more public or intellectual.

lesson.pronunciationTip: 논쟁 is written nonjaeng. Use audio and Hangul together because romanization is only a helper.

entries.shortExplanation: 설득 means "persuasion" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 설득 (seoldeuk) means "persuasion". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 설득을 하다 ("to persuade"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 설득 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 설득을 하다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 설득.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 하다 form; 설득하다 is the common one-word verb (설득하다 = to persuade someone).
성공하다 ('succeed') and 실패하다 ('fail') pair naturally with 설득.
설득 + 력 (power); 설득력이 있다 = to be persuasive.
당하다 makes the passive: ended up being convinced by someone.

examples.ko: 부모님을 설득하는 데 시간이 오래 걸렸어요.
examples.romanization: bumonimeul seoldeukaneun de sigani orae geollyeosseoyo.
examples.en: It took a long time to persuade my parents.
examples.note: 설득하는 데 시간이 걸리다 = 'it takes time to persuade'; 데 = 'in the process of'.

examples.en: That person's argument is persuasive.
examples.note: 설득력이 있다 = 'to have persuasive power', a key intermediate phrase.

examples.ko: 아무리 설득해도 그는 마음을 바꾸지 않았어요.
examples.romanization: amuri seoldeukaedo geuneun maeumeul bakkuji anasseoyo.
examples.en: No matter how much I tried to persuade him, he didn't change his mind.
examples.note: 아무리 ~해도 = 'no matter how much ~'; 마음을 바꾸다 = 'change one's mind'.

entries.nuance: 설득 is the act of persuading someone to accept your view or do something, usually through reasoning rather than force. The derived noun 설득력 ('persuasiveness') is extremely common — Koreans judge arguments by whether 설득력이 있다 or 없다. Note that 설득하다 takes the person as its object (사람을 설득하다), unlike English 'persuade someone of something'.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 설득 (persuading by reason) with 강요 (forcing/coercion); 설득 wins agreement, 강요 imposes against the will.
Forgetting that 설득하다 takes a person object — say 친구를 설득했어요, not 친구에게 설득했어요.

entries.explanation: "negotiation" is 협상 (hyeopsang). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 협상을 하다 ("to negotiate"). Watch the particle attached to 협상 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 협상을 하다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 협상.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 하다 form; 협상하다 also works as a single verb.
결렬되다 ('break down') is the standard news verb for failed talks.

usagePhrases.en: negotiations are concluded / reach a deal
usagePhrases.note: 타결되다 ('be settled') is the counterpart for a successful outcome.
협상 테이블에 앉다 = 'sit at the negotiating table', a common idiom.

examples.ko: 두 회사는 가격을 두고 오랫동안 협상을 했어요.
examples.romanization: du hoesaneun gagyeogeul dugo oraetdongan hyeopsangeul haesseoyo.
examples.en: The two companies negotiated over the price for a long time.
examples.note: ~을/를 두고 협상하다 = 'negotiate over ~'; 오랫동안 = 'for a long time'.

examples.en: The wage negotiations ultimately broke down.

examples.ko: 양측은 며칠간의 협상 끝에 합의에 이르렀어요.
examples.romanization: yangcheugeun myeochilganui hyeopsang kkeute habuie ireureosseoyo.
examples.en: After several days of negotiation, both sides reached an agreement.
examples.note: 협상 끝에 = 'after negotiation'; 합의에 이르다 = 'reach an agreement'.

entries.nuance: 협상 is formal negotiation between parties with differing interests — business deals, labor talks, or diplomacy — aiming for a mutually acceptable compromise. It is more structured and higher-stakes than everyday 흥정 (haggling over a price). News reports describe its outcome with the fixed pair 타결되다 (reach a deal) versus 결렬되다 (break down).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Using 협상 for casual price haggling at a market — that is 흥정, while 협상 is formal, often institutional.
Mixing up 타결 (a successful settlement) and 결렬 (a breakdown); they are opposite outcomes of 협상.

entries.shortExplanation: 연설 means "speech; public address" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 연설 (yeonseol) = "speech; public address". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 연설을 하다 ("to give a speech") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 연설, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 연설을 하다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 연설.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 하다 is the standard verb; 연설하다 also works.
연설 + 문 (writing); the written script of an address.
취임 ('taking office') + 연설; a common fixed compound.
감동적이다 ('moving') is a natural modifier for a memorable address.

examples.ko: 대통령은 국민 앞에서 짧은 연설을 했어요.
examples.romanization: daetongnyeongeun gungmin apeseo jjalbeun yeonseoreul haesseoyo.
examples.en: The president gave a short speech before the people.
examples.note: 국민 앞에서 = 'before the people'; 연설을 하다 = 'give a speech'.

examples.en: His graduation speech was truly moving.
A good speech moves the hearts of the audience.

entries.nuance: 연설 is a formal spoken address delivered to an audience — by a politician, a graduate, or a public figure — usually prepared in advance. It differs from 발표 (a presentation of information or results) and from 강의 (a lecture meant to teach). Use 연설 when the emphasis is on a prepared, often inspiring public address.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 연설 (a public speech/address) with 발표 (a presentation, e.g. of a project or findings).
Using 연설 for an informal toast or few words at a small gathering — for that say 인사말 ('a few words of greeting').

entries.shortExplanation: 강의 means "lecture; (university) course" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 강의 (gangui) means "lecture; (university) course". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 강의를 듣다 ("to take / attend a lecture"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 강의 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 강의를 듣다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 강의.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 듣다 ('listen') is the idiomatic verb — you 'hear' a lecture or course.
From the teacher's side; 강의하다 also works as one verb.
온라인 강의 became extremely common; also 인터넷 강의 (인강).
강의 + 실 (room); the room where a lecture is held.

examples.ko: 이번 학기에 한국 역사 강의를 듣고 있어요.
examples.romanization: ibeon hakgie hanguk yeoksa ganguireul deutgo isseoyo.
examples.en: This semester I'm taking a Korean history course.
examples.note: 강의를 듣다 = 'take a course'; ~고 있다 = ongoing action.

examples.ko: 그 교수님의 강의는 항상 인기가 많아요.
examples.romanization: geu gyosunimui ganguineun hangsang ingiga manayo.
examples.en: That professor's lectures are always very popular.

examples.ko: 요즘은 집에서 온라인 강의를 들을 수 있어요.
examples.romanization: yojeumeun jibeseo ollain ganguireul deureul su isseoyo.
examples.en: These days you can take online lectures from home.

entries.nuance: 강의 means a lecture or an academic course, especially at the university level, where a teacher presents material to students. Note the idiom 강의를 듣다 ('listen to a lecture') for attending or taking a course — you do not 받다 or 배우다 a 강의. It is more formal and content-focused than 수업, which is the general word for a class at any level.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Saying 강의를 받다 or 강의를 배우다 for 'take a lecture' — the correct verb is 강의를 듣다.
Using 강의 for an elementary or middle-school class; 강의 leans academic/university, while 수업 is the general word for any class.

entries.shortExplanation: 인터뷰 means "interview" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "interview" is 인터뷰 (inteobyu). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 인터뷰를 하다 ("to do / conduct an interview"). Watch the particle attached to 인터뷰 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 인터뷰를 하다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 인터뷰.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 하다 form; used for both the interviewer and interviewee side.

usagePhrases.en: to agree to / give an interview
usagePhrases.note: 응하다 ('comply, respond to') is the formal verb for accepting an interview.
인터뷰 + 기사 (article); a written piece based on an interview.
방송 ('broadcast') marks the medium of the interview.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 방송에서 솔직한 인터뷰를 했어요.
examples.romanization: geu baeuneun bangsongeseo soljikan inteobyureul haesseoyo.
examples.en: That actor gave an honest interview on the broadcast.
A reporter conducted interviews with citizens in the street.
examples.note: 인터뷰를 진행하다 = 'conduct an interview'; 거리에서 = 'in the street'.

examples.ko: 취업 준비를 하면서 면접 인터뷰 연습을 많이 했어요.
examples.romanization: chwieop junbireul hamyeonseo myeonjeop inteobyu yeonseubeul mani haesseoyo.
examples.en: While preparing for jobs, I practiced a lot for job interviews.

entries.nuance: 인터뷰 is a loanword covering both media interviews (a reporter questioning someone) and the question-and-answer of getting a story or opinion. For a job interview, Koreans more often use the native term 면접, though 면접 인터뷰 and 인터뷰 are also heard. Use 인터뷰 when the focus is press, broadcast, or research questioning rather than a hiring evaluation.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Defaulting to 인터뷰 for a job interview — the more standard word in Korea is 면접.
Saying 인터뷰를 받다 for 'be interviewed'; Koreans say 인터뷰를 하다 or 인터뷰에 응하다.

entries.shortExplanation: 방송 means "broadcast; (a TV/radio) program" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 방송 (bangsong) = "broadcast; (a TV/radio) program". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 방송에 나오다 ("to appear on a broadcast / be on TV") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 방송, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 방송에 나오다. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 방송.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.en: to appear on a broadcast / be on TV
usagePhrases.note: 나오다 ('come out') = to appear on air; 방송에 나가다 = to go on air.
생 ('raw, live') + 방송; a real-time broadcast.
방송 + 국 (bureau/station); the company that broadcasts.

usagePhrases.en: to make it onto a broadcast
usagePhrases.note: 타다 ('ride') idiomatically = to get aired / go viral on TV.

examples.ko: 그 식당은 방송에 나온 뒤로 손님이 많아졌어요.
examples.romanization: geu sikdangeun bangsonge naon dwiro sonnimi manajyeosseoyo.
examples.en: That restaurant got busier after appearing on a broadcast.
examples.note: 방송에 나오다 = 'appear on TV'; ~ㄴ 뒤로 = 'ever since'.

examples.ko: 이 프로그램은 매주 금요일 저녁에 생방송으로 진행돼요.
examples.romanization: i peurogeuraemeun maeju geumyoil jeonyeoge saengbangsongeuro jinhaengdwaeyo.
examples.en: This program airs live every Friday evening.

examples.ko: 방송에서 본 요리를 직접 따라 만들어 봤어요.
examples.romanization: bangsongeseo bon yorireul jikjeop ttara mandeureo bwasseoyo.
examples.en: I tried making a dish I saw on a broadcast myself.
examples.note: 방송에서 보다 = 'see on TV'; 따라 만들다 = 'make by following'.

entries.nuance: 방송 covers both the act of broadcasting and a specific TV or radio program. The idiom 방송을 타다 ('ride the broadcast') is a vivid way to say something got aired and gained attention. It pairs with 나오다/나가다 for appearing on air. Note 생방송 (live) versus 녹화 방송 (pre-recorded) is a useful contrast.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 방송 (a broadcast/program) with 채널 ('channel') or 프로그램 — 방송 is the airing itself.
Saying 방송을 보다 when you mean a specific show; that is fine casually, but for a named program 프로그램 is clearer.

examples.ko: 최근 여론조사에서 그 정책에 대한 반대가 높게 나왔어요.

entries.nuance: 여론 is public opinion — the collective views and mood of society on an issue, especially as measured by polls or reflected in the media. commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.

entries.nuance: 언론 refers to the press or the news media as a social institution — newspapers, broadcasters, and journalists collectively, along with their role in informing the public. usagePhrases.note: 뜨다 ('come up, pop up') is natural for a post showing up.

examples.en: A new notice was posted on the company board.
examples.note: 게시판에 올라오다 = 'be posted on the board'; 공지 = 'notice'.

examples.ko: 궁금한 점이 있으면 자유게시판에 글을 남기세요.
examples.romanization: gunggeumhan jeomi isseumyeon jayugesipane geureul namgiseyo.
examples.en: If you have questions, leave a post on the open board.
examples.note: 글을 남기다 = 'leave a post'; 궁금한 점 = 'something you're curious about'.

examples.romanization: geu geuri gesipaneseo keun hwajega doeeosseoyo.

examples.note: 화제가 되다 = 'become a topic'; 게시판에서 = 'on the board'.

entries.nuance: 게시판 is a bulletin board, both the physical kind (a notice board on a wall) and the online kind (a forum or message board on a website). Online, you 글을 올리다 ('upload a post') or 글을 남기다 ('leave a post') on a 게시판, and others reply with 댓글 ('comments'). It is the structured posting space, distinct from a live 채팅 (chat).
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Confusing 게시판 (the board where posts live) with 댓글 (the comments under a post).
Saying 게시판에 쓰다 alone for posting online; the idiomatic phrasing is 게시판에 글을 올리다/남기다.

examples.en: I read an interesting article in today's newspaper.

examples.romanization: geu sageone daehan gisaga modeun sinmune nasseoyo.
examples.en: An article about that incident came out in every newspaper.

entries.nuance: 기사 means a news article or report — a single written piece of journalism, whether in a newspaper, magazine, or online. It is the concrete unit of content, distinct from 언론 (the press as an institution) and 보도 (the act of reporting). Note that 기사 is a homonym: it also means 'driver' (운전기사), so context decides the meaning.

Using 기사 for the abstract media institution; that is 언론, while 기사 is one specific article.

usagePhrases.en: to be responsible / to bear responsibility
usagePhrases.note: the core pattern; 책임이 있다 means the duty rests on you
set phrase with 지다 to carry; this is how you say you will own the outcome
add -감 to mean the inner feeling of being responsible, used to describe a person
add -자 for the responsible party, e.g. the manager handling an issue

examples.ko: 이 일은 제가 맡았으니까 끝까지 책임을 지겠습니다.
examples.romanization: i ireun jega matasseunikka kkeutkkaji chaegimeul jigetseumnida.
examples.en: Since I took on this work, I will take responsibility for it to the end.
examples.note: formal 합니다 form; common at work when committing to a task

examples.en: Parents have a responsibility toward their children.
examples.note: N에 대한 책임 marks who or what the responsibility is for

examples.en: You should not push responsibility onto others.
examples.note: 책임을 미루다 means to shift blame or duty away

entries.nuance: 책임 is the abstract weight of being answerable for something, and it lives mainly through verbs: 책임을 지다 (take it on) and 책임이 있다 (it falls on you). Note that 책임 is the bare noun, while the already-common 책임감 specifically names the inner sense of duty a person feels. Use 책임 for the obligation itself and 책임감 when describing someone's character.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Do not say 책임하다 — 책임 is not a verb; use 책임을 지다 instead.
Do not swap 책임 with 의무; 책임 is being answerable for an outcome, while 의무 is a duty you are required to perform.

entries.nuance: 의무 is a duty imposed from outside, by law, rules, or a role, that you are required to carry out, and it is often paired with 권리 (rights) as its natural opposite. commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Do not use 의무 for a casual favor; it implies a binding requirement, not a friendly request.
Do not confuse 의무 with 책임; 의무 is a required duty, while 책임 is accountability for an outcome.

Do not say 권리하다 — express it with verbs like 권리를 주장하다 or 권리가 있다.

entries.nuance: 의지 is willpower, the inner determination to push through difficulty, and it is most often described as 강하다 (strong) or 약하다 (weak). It is about resolve and self-control, not a casual wish, so it carries a sense of effort against temptation or hardship. Note this is the homophone meaning will; the verb 의지하다 (to rely on someone) is a separate, related word.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Do not confuse the noun 의지 (willpower) with the verb 의지하다 (to lean on / rely on someone).
Do not use 의지 for a light wish like wanting a snack; use it for serious determination.

정신이 없다 does not mean having no mind; it means being frazzled or swamped.

entries.nuance: 상상 is imagination, the act of forming pictures or scenarios in your mind, and it becomes a verb as 상상하다. entries.explanation: "judgment, decision" is 판단 (pandan). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 판단하다 ("to judge / to determine"). usagePhrases.en: to make a judgment / reach a decision
usagePhrases.note: set phrase with 내리다; sounds deliberate and weighty
add -력 for the ability to judge well
올바른 + 판단 for a right decision, common in advice

examples.romanization: seonggeupage pandanhaji malgo kkeutkkaji deureo boseyo.

entries.nuance: 판단 is the act of weighing a situation and forming a conclusion, the mental step of assessing before deciding. Do not confuse 판단 (assessing and deciding) with 결정 (the final choice itself); 판단 emphasizes the reasoning behind the choice.
Do not say 판단이 하다; the verb is 판단하다 or the phrase 판단을 내리다.

entries.explanation: 성실하다 (seongsilhada) means "sincere, diligent, conscientious". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 성실한 사람 ("a diligent, dependable person"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 성실하다 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. 태도 (attitude) is praised more than raw talent in Korea
성실히 = slightly more formal adverb, common in written praise

examples.ko: 저는 무슨 일이든 성실하게 하려고 노력해요.
examples.romanization: jeoneun museun irideun seongsilhage haryeogo noryeokaeyo.
examples.en: I try to do everything diligently, whatever it is.
examples.note: Safe, strong self-PR line for interviews; 무슨 일이든 = whatever the task

examples.en: That employee is so conscientious that the boss trusts them most.
examples.note: 믿다 = trust; 성실 is closely tied to being trusted

examples.en: We gave an award to the student who attended faithfully.
examples.note: 출석하다 = attend; 성실 covers showing up consistently

entries.nuance: 성실하다 is one of the most valued personality words in Korean work and school culture — it means sincere, diligent, and reliable in carrying out duties, the kind of steady person who shows up and follows through. It's about earnest effort and consistency rather than results, so it's the single safest strength to claim in an interview. Don't confuse it with 정직하다 (honest/truthful): 성실 is about diligence, 정직 is about not lying.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Stem is 성실하다, so conjugate 성실해요 / 성실한 — never 성실하해요
Don't use it to mean 'honest'; that overlapping-but-different idea is 정직하다

Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 침착한 사람 ("a composed, unflappable person"). entries.nuance: 침착하다 means composed and unflappable, especially the ability to stay calm under pressure or in an emergency — it's almost always a compliment and a top trait to claim for high-stress jobs. It overlaps with 차분하다 (calm/settled), but 침착하다 leans specifically on keeping it together in a crisis, while 차분하다 describes a generally quiet, steady temperament. Unlike 냉정하다, there's no cold/detached undertone.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Stem is 침착하다 → 침착해요 / 침착한, not 침착하해요
Don't swap it freely with 차분하다 in a crisis: 침착하다 is composure under pressure; 차분하다 is a calm baseline temperament

It conjugates as 이기적이에요 / 이기적인 / 이기적으로.

Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 정중하게 부탁하다 ("ask politely/respectfully"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 정중하다 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.

entries.nuance: 정중하다 means courteous and respectful in a formal, dignified way — proper manners and respectful language, a notch more formal than 친절하다 (kind/friendly). You'd describe staff toward important guests, a careful apology, or a polite refusal as 정중하다, where 친절하다 would feel too casual-warm. It's about showing respect through form, not personal warmth.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Don't swap it with 친절하다 (warm/friendly kindness); 정중하다 is formal respect/courtesy
Stem is 정중하다 → 정중해요 / 정중한 / 정중하게, never 정중하해요

entries.shortExplanation: 우유부단하다 means "indecisive, wishy-washy, unable to make up one's mind" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 우유부단하다 (uyubudanhada) = "indecisive, wishy-washy, unable to make up one's mind". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 우유부단한 사람 ("an indecisive person") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 우유부단하다, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.

examples.romanization: jeoneun uyubudanhaeseo menyu goreuneun dedo hancham geollyeoyo.
examples.en: I'm so indecisive that even picking off a menu takes me ages.
examples.note: Relatable everyday example; 한참 = a long while

examples.en: I dithered indecisively and missed a good opportunity.
examples.note: 망설이다 = hesitate; 기회를 놓치다 = miss a chance

examples.en: When a leader is indecisive, the team struggles.

entries.nuance: 우유부단하다 is a four-character Sino-Korean word (優柔不斷) meaning indecisive and wishy-washy — chronically unable to make up your mind or commit to a choice. It's the negative flip side of 신중하다 (prudent): 신중하다 weighs things wisely, but 우유부단하다 just can't decide. It's a common, slightly self-deprecating way people describe themselves when they agonize over small choices.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
It functions as a 하다-adjective: 우유부단해요 / 우유부단한, not 우유부단이에요
Don't mix it up with 신중하다 (carefully prudent); 우유부단 is failing to decide, not wise caution

entries.shortExplanation: 정확하다 means "to be accurate, exact, correct" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 정확하다 (jeonghwakada) means "to be accurate, exact, correct". Learn it inside a frame, not as a bare word: a useful first chunk is 정확한 ("accurate (+ noun)"). In Korean the particle or ending next to 정확하다 signals its job — topic, subject, object, place, time, method, or description — so read the examples for the small piece beside it. Start with one real sentence about basic everyday communication, then change a single part.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 정확한. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 정확하다.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: Modifier form: 정확한 정보 'accurate information', 정확한 시간 'the exact time'.
Polite present. 하다 verbs drop 하 and add 해요.
Both adverb forms are common; 정확히 sounds slightly more written.
Negative; often used as 정확하지 않아요 to soften 'that's wrong'.

examples.ko: 이 번역이 정확한지 한번 확인해 주세요.
examples.romanization: i beonyeogi jeonghwakanji hanbeon hwaginhae juseyo.
examples.en: Please check once whether this translation is accurate.
Thank you for keeping the time exactly.
If my memory is accurate, the meeting was at 3.

entries.nuance: 정확하다 is about matching the truth or a standard with no error — accurate numbers, correct facts, precise timing. It overlaps with 맞다 ('be right') but is more formal and emphasizes precision rather than just being acceptable. Use it for data, translations, pronunciation, and measurements.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
Do not confuse with 확실하다 ('be certain/sure'); 정확하다 is about correctness, 확실하다 is about confidence/certainty.
Avoid '정확하다 정보' — use the modifier form 정확한 정보.

lesson.canDo: Use 정확하다 inside a real beginner sentence, not only as an isolated translation.
studyFlow: Say the word first: 정확하다. Check the romanization only after trying the Hangul.
Memorize one useful chunk: 정확한.
Notice which particle, place marker, or ending appears around the word.
Make one personal sentence by changing only one noun, place, time, or adjective.
lesson.teacherNote: 정확하다 should be taught as a sentence ingredient. The student needs the common frame more than a dictionary definition.
lesson.pronunciationTip: 정확하다 is written jeonghwakada. Use audio and Hangul together because romanization is only a helper.

entries.shortExplanation: 자세하다 means "to be detailed, in detail" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: "to be detailed, in detail" is 자세하다 (jasehada). The word itself is easy; what matters is the company it keeps, like 자세한 ("detailed (+ noun)"). Watch the particle attached to 자세하다 in each example — that little marker, not the word, tells you whether it is the topic, the subject, the object, or a place. Copy one full sentence about basic everyday communication first, then vary one word.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 자세한. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 자세하다.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 자세한 설명 'a detailed explanation', 자세한 내용 'detailed content'.
Polite present, though the adverb 자세히 is used far more often.
The go-to adverb form: 자세히 설명하다 'explain in detail'.
Common request phrase in conversation and email.

examples.ko: 이 부분을 좀 더 자세히 설명해 주시겠어요?
examples.romanization: i bubuneul jom deo jasehi seolmyeonghae jusigesseoyo?
examples.en: Could you explain this part in a bit more detail?
examples.note: 자세히 + 설명하다 is a fixed collocation.

examples.en: I'll send the detailed schedule by email.
Read the contract carefully before you sign.

entries.nuance: 자세하다 describes something that includes a lot of specific detail, and its adverb 자세히 also means doing something closely/thoroughly (reading, looking). In speech you will hear 자세히 (adverb) much more than the plain adjective. It is the natural word for asking someone to elaborate.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
The adverb is 자세히 (with ㅣ), not 자세하게 in most everyday phrases — both exist, but 자세히 is far more idiomatic.
Don't use it to mean 'careful' in the sense of caution; that is 조심하다.

entries.shortExplanation: 적절하다 means "to be appropriate, suitable, apt" and is learned through practical beginner sentence frames.
entries.explanation: 적절하다 (jeokjeolhada) = "to be appropriate, suitable, apt". Treat it as a building block that needs a frame: 적절한 ("appropriate (+ noun)") shows how it actually behaves. The grammar lives in the particle or ending beside 적절하다, so notice that piece as you read, not just the dictionary meaning. Begin from a complete sentence about basic everyday communication and swap just one element to make it yours.
entries.learnerPriority: First memorize 적절한. Then read the examples and notice the particle or ending attached near 적절하다.
entries.contextHint: Use this word when talking about basic everyday communication. The examples show whether it naturally works with 은/는, 이/가, 을/를, 에, 에서, 로/으로, or a descriptive ending.

usagePhrases.note: 적절한 표현 'an appropriate expression', 적절한 대응 'an appropriate response'.
Polite present; common in feedback and evaluations.

examples.ko: 그 상황에서는 그 말이 적절하지 않았어요.
examples.romanization: geu sanghwangeseoneun geu mari jeokjeolhaji anasseoyo.
examples.en: In that situation, those words weren't appropriate.
We are looking for an appropriate solution to the problem.
The price was reasonable, so I signed right away.

entries.nuance: 적절하다 means well-suited to the situation, context, or purpose — the 'right' choice given the circumstances. It is more formal and judgment-oriented than 맞다, and is common in writing, work, and evaluations (e.g., an appropriate word, response, or measure). It carries a sense of social/contextual fit.
commonMistakes: Do not memorize this only as an English translation; memorize one Korean sentence frame.
적절하다 vs 적당하다: 적절하다 = 'fitting/apt for the context'; 적당하다 = 'a moderate/just-right amount or degree' (and can be casual). They are not always interchangeable.
Use 적절한 (modifier) before a noun, not 적절하다.
